subject: ClearWallet: sudden 5xx spike + reserved throughput depletion
messages:
From: Jake Taylor <j.taylor@clearwallet.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@clearwallet.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 07:43:00 -0800
Subject: Immediate: production 5xx surge + reserved capacity drain

Team —

We're seeing a sudden, sustained spike in 5xx errors across our /generate endpoints starting ~07:20 PST. Latency has jumped from median 120ms to >1.2s and our reserved throughput units appear to be exhausted for the past 15 minutes (we're getting rate_limited responses with 429/503). This is impacting checkout flows for ~6% of live traffic.

Attached: sample 5xx logs and a screenshot of the dashboard.

We've already switched a subset of traffic to a queued retry on our side, but this is not sustainable. Can you confirm whether this is a capacity issue in the dedicated pool or a model/runtime regression? We need a mitigation path in the next 30m and a remediation plan.

-Jake
Jake Taylor
CTO, ClearWallet
j.taylor@clearwallet.com
+1 415-555-0199

Attachment: clearwallet_5xx_sample.log (text log)
Attachment: cw_dashboard_1117.png (png)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Taylor <j.taylor@clearwallet.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 07:50:22 -08:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: production 5xx surge + reserved capacity drain

Jake — thanks for the ping and logs. We're on it.

Immediate notes:
- I can confirm we're seeing an elevated queue depth from ClearWallet's reservation ID in our monitoring.
- Early signal suggests aggressive long-context requests from a small percentage of sessions are inflating per-request token use and triggering headroom exhaustion in the dedicated pool.

Actions I'm initiating now:
1) Routing policy: ask to temporarily route ~30% of ClearWallet traffic to their hosted fallback model variant to reduce pressure.
2) Apply an emergency soft-rate-limit on very long requests ( >30k token window) for the next 45m.
3) Priyom, please pull a live pool snapshot and confirm if we have reclaimable headroom or available burst nodes in the region.

David will coordinate the customer call — I'll stay on the thread for the tech details.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:02:10 -08:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: production 5xx surge + reserved capacity drain — pool snapshot & mitigations

Summary of what I see (live snapshot at 08:00 PST):
- Dedicated pool us-west-2 / pool-42 is at 98% GPU utilization and queue depth is 3.4x typical for this timeslot.
- There are ~12 long-lived sessions ( > 20k token ephemeral KV) consuming ~28% of token-processing capacity.
- No kernel regressions noted; model variant latency profiles are within expected ranges.

Immediate recommended playbook (30-60m):
1) Route 35% of ClearWallet requests to hosted fallback model variant (lower-cost, smaller context) — quick config change I can push now.
2) Apply soft per-request token cutoff at 25k for ClearWallet's reservation ID with transparent 429 + Retry-After in header to give clients a signal.
3) Enable conservative preemption on the dedicated pool to free up 2 nodes for churn-heavy sessions. Priyom->ops to trigger preemption now.
4) Start a temporary burst allocation: request + provision 2 g4dnx instances in us-west-2 as emergency headroom (30–60m bootstrap).

I can push 1 & 2 in the next 5m. Spinning burst nodes is dependent on infra quota; David / Marissa can approve emergency spend/credits if needed.

Priyom Das
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Taylor <j.taylor@clearwallet.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:10:35 -08:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: production 5xx surge + reserved capacity drain — short-term mitigation

Jake — quick update and plan for the next 30 minutes: 

What we've done so far:
- Enabled routing of ~35% traffic to hosted fallback (should reduce pressure in ~3m).
- Applied a temporary soft cutoff at 25k tokens for long requests (Retroactive 429 + Retry-After header).
- Priyom kicked off preemption to free two nodes and requested burst nodes from infra.

Next steps / ask of ClearWallet:
- If you can reduce very long-context calls client-side (e.g. trim conversation state for background jobs) that will immediately lower token consumption.
- Please join a 30-minute call at 08:15 PST so we can walk through telemetry and agree on a recovery timeline.

As a gesture for the disruption and the immediate operational effort, we'll provision a one-time credit to offset ClearWallet's overages for today's incident window (details to follow after postmortem).

Joining the call: https://meet.redwood.ai/clearwallet-incident-08-15

-David
David Kim
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Post-incident note + exec flag for ClearWallet incident (Nov 17)

Team —

Thanks for the quick response. Post-call summary: we reduced headroom pressure and error rates are trending back to baseline after routing & preemption, but this incident exposed two product gaps:

1) Reservation isolation: current heuristics don't prevent headroom starvation when a small subset of sessions uses extreme contexts. We need a short-term enforcement knob and a medium-term quota segmentation change.
2) Emergency burst: provisioning burst nodes takes too long under infra quota checks. We should pre-authorize a small emergency pool for top-tier reserved customers.

As an exec ask: Vivek, we need a quick approval (email OK) to spin up temporary capacity and to make a one-time credit for ClearWallet effective immediately. This will both remediate and preserve the account relationship while we implement the two product fixes above.

I'll own a postmortem and a prioritized backlog item for the quota/segmentation fixes. Rishi — please record the customer impact numbers and include in the postmortem: % of requests affected, avg extra latency, and estimated revenue impact for the 2-hour window.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
